newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN to admit Burma, Laos, Cambodia at same time.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN to admit Burma, Laos, Cambodia at same time.

text.p: ASEAN leaders agreed that Burma, Cambodia and Laos should join the seven-nation Southeast Asian group simultaneously, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Saturday.
But he did not disclose the timing, despite the fact Cambodia and Laos had been expected to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations next July.

"The heads of government reaffirmed their strong commitment to the speedy realisation of an ASEAN comprising all 10 Southeast Asian countries. They agreed that Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar (Burma) be admitted as ASEAN members simultaneously," he said at the end of a one-day ASEAN summit in Jakarta
"As to the actual timing of the admission of the three countries, this will be announced in due time," he told a news conference.
ASEAN currently groups Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam, Singapore and Brunei as full members.
Burma joined Laos and Cambodia as an observer last July.
Like the other two, Burma has applied for membership, but a question mark has hung over the timing following bitter Western criticism of the Rangoon government over its human rights and democracy.
Alatas said the ASEAN leaders agreed "to request the relevant ASEAN bodies to continue with the necessary technical and procedural steps" to admit the three countries.
He said all three would participate in ASEAN activities.
Questioned about the timing of the admission, he repeated that this would be disclosed in due course.

Asked if there had been any split among ASEAN leaders over admitting Burma, he replied: "There is no difference among ASEAN as to the principle of Myanmar's entry into ASEAN. Everyone agrees Myanmar should become a full member of ASEAN."
The only difference was over the timing, he said.
